title: Your fridge doesn’t make cold, it pumps heat into your kitchen
body: Cold is just a lack of heat, so a fridge cools food by carrying heat out of the box. A refrigerant flows round a sealed loop: a narrow valve drops its pressure so it turns colder than the food and soaks up heat, then a compressor squeezes it until it is hotter than the kitchen and it sheds that heat through coils outside. Heat only flows from warmer to colder on its own, and the compressor’s work is what lets it be carried the other way. That is why the coils at the back or sides of a fridge feel warm.

slides.alt: Animated cutaway diagram of a fridge. Refrigerant dots, coloured from icy blue to hot orange, flow round a sealed loop through the compressor, the hot coils at the back, a narrow valve and the cold coils inside, while heat squiggles move from the food into the cold coils and out of the hot ones.

slides.heading: Why squeezing makes it hot
slides.text: Compressing a gas raises its pressure and its temperature. Now hotter than the kitchen air, the gas sheds heat as it flows through the coils, cooling until it condenses back into a liquid.

slides.heading: Why the valve makes it icy
slides.text: Forced through a narrow valve, the liquid’s pressure falls suddenly and part of it boils at once. That boiling draws heat from the rest, so the mix comes out colder than the inside of the fridge.

slides.heading: The refrigerant’s journey, starting inside
items: Boils in the cold coils inside
slides.explanation: It soaks up heat as it boils inside, the compressor makes it hot enough to shed that heat outside, and the valve drops its pressure to make it cold again.

left.label: Myth
left.text: A fridge makes cold and blows it into the box.

right.label: Fact
right.text: A fridge takes heat out of the box and gives it off to the room through its coils.

slides.question: You leave the fridge door open in a closed kitchen. What happens to the kitchen’s temperature?
slides.explanation: The heat the fridge takes in goes straight back out into the same room through its coils, plus the energy its motor uses. So the room ends up a little warmer.

slides.heading: Same trick, other machines
slides.text: Air conditioners and heat pumps use the same vapour-compression cycle. A heat pump runs it to warm a house, carrying heat in from the colder air outside.
